frozenBy: T264P (owner-approved issue #264, planning-review correction; hard prerequisite for T264C)
purpose: Freeze the provenance and correlation rule for every raster variant an adaptive second analysis may observe, before T264C exists. The file declares where each variant's pixels come from, which variants are correlated because they share one rendering, which variants are independent because they are separate renderings, and how many independent groups an agreement claim needs. No variant raster is produced or measured here.

document.note: Both the analytic fixture path and the corpus path carry byte-identical PDFs (same SHA-256). Every variant below is rendered from this one document, so every variant is glyph-correlated with every other variant of the same page.

hashConvention.sourceDocumentSha256: SHA-256 of the PDF bytes, declared by the ground truth and recomputed in `test_adaptive_provenance.py`.
hashConvention.sourceRasterSha256: SHA-256 over the exact raster bytes the variant's rendering produced, before any degradation. Recorded at capture time; a raster that is not in the tree stays `PENDING_RUN`.
hashConvention.variantRasterSha256: SHA-256 over the exact raster bytes delivered to the OCR port after the degradation chain. Recorded at capture time; a raster that is not in the tree stays `PENDING_RUN`.
hashConvention.failClosed: A variant with `PENDING_RUN` hashes produces no evidence row and may not be counted in an agreement claim. Nothing here may be filled in from memory or from a re-render after the fact.

The representative is the first member in the producer's declaration order because the group has no undegraded member.

correlationRule.rule: Two image variants are correlated when they descend from the same rendering of a page: the same renderer, the same capture resolution, and the same source bytes. Degradations (contrast stretch, shadow, JPEG round trip, deskew, skew) transform one rendering and stay in its correlation group. Two renderings of the same document are separate groups at raster level, but they are still one document, so glyph and content claims never become independent that way.
correlationRule.policyRule: Every adaptive variant derives from the same original page scan and is correlated evidence.
correlationRule.groupDefinition: A `correlationGroup` is the set of variants whose pixels come from one rendering event. Membership is declared per variant and cross-checked against `correlationGroups[].members`; two groups may never share a `pixelSourceId`.
correlationRule.independentDefinition: `independent: true` marks the declared representative of a correlation group: the variant whose raster is the rendering itself rather than a transformation of another declared variant. `false` marks every member whose pixels are derived from another declared variant in the same group. The flag never creates a second evidence slot for a group.
correlationRule.countingRule: Observations are counted per correlation group, not per variant: `independentGroups = |{correlationGroup(v) : v selected}|`. Selecting three degradations of one capture yields one group; selecting the reference raster and its contrast stretch yields one group.

glyphLevelCollapse.scope: character, glyph, umlaut, currency, and content claims
glyphLevelCollapse.rule: Every variant in this file renders the same document, so a character that the font, the encoding, or the OCR model cannot produce fails in every variant. A special-character, umlaut, currency, or content claim therefore has exactly one independent group per document, and no combination of these variants may claim otherwise.

correlationRule.failClosed: If the derivation of a variant cannot be resolved to a declared source node or declared variant, the variant is dropped instead of being counted as independent.

excludedVariants.reason: The analysis contract is fixed at 200 DPI with an exact `RasterSize`, the raster port has no crop request, and the documented 4096 px cap silently downscales. A 2x region render would either change the analysis scale or silently lose resolution, so it is excluded from v1 and may not be added as an independent group without its own contract change and a measured pixel-identity proof.

decisionRule.counting: independentGroups = number of distinct `correlationGroup` values in the selected observation set; the number of observations is never the evidence count
decisionRule.insufficientGroupsOutcome: If the selected observations reach fewer than `minIndependentGroups` correlation groups, the result is correlation-limited: the pass reports one observation per group, does not raise `twoIndependentOcrLinesAgree`, does not apply the independent-OCR confidence bonus, and never auto-confirms. A repeated group cannot justify a further pass on its own.
decisionRule.hashGate: A variant whose `variantRasterSha256` is `PENDING_RUN` (or whose `derivedFrom` does not resolve) produces no evidence row, so it can never contribute to `independentGroups`.
decisionRule.perDocumentCap: All variants of one source document contribute at most one independent group to a glyph or content claim (`correlationRule.glyphLevelCollapse`).
decisionRule.unchanged: This rule adds no trigger, threshold, bound, or acceptance value. `tools/evaluation/adaptive-policy.v1.json` stays byte-identical and is hash-bound below.

policyArtifact.relationship: Consumed, never edited. The policy owns the numeric triggers, hysteresis, pass/time/memory bounds, render strategy, and A/B/C acceptance thresholds; this file only declares where variant pixels come from and how their observations may be counted.
